title: From 100 Miles to 400: How Electric Cars Quietly Became Practical
title_zh: 从100英里到400英里：电动汽车如何悄然变得实用
intro_zh: 本文约551词，围绕电动汽车如何从新奇事物走入日常生活展开，包含6个CET-4核心词，适合四级阅读训练。

paragraphs.en: On a quiet morning in a Chinese city, a driver unplugs a small cable from the wall, slides into the car, and leaves without the rumble of an engine. Ten years ago, this scene belonged to car shows and science magazines. Today, it is part of ordinary life. Electric cars have moved from curiosity to daily transport, changing how people think about fuel, noise, and the road itself.
paragraphs.zh: 在中国一座城市安静的早晨，一位司机从墙上拔下小充电线，坐进车里，没有发动机的轰鸣便出发了。十年前，这一幕只属于车展和科普杂志。如今，它已是日常生活的一部分。电动汽车已从新奇事物变成日常交通工具，改变着人们对燃料、噪音和道路本身的看法。

paragraphs.en: The shift is visible in numbers. In 2023, nearly 14 million electric cars were sold worldwide, about 18 percent of all new cars. China, Europe, and the United States led the way. Families did not adopt them because of fashion alone. Lower running costs, quieter cabins, and government support made the choice easier. What once felt like a risk now feels like a sensible purchase for many households.
paragraphs.zh: 这种转变在数字中清晰可见。2023年，全球售出近1400万辆电动汽车，约占全部新车的18%。中国、欧洲和美国走在前列。家庭选择它们并非只图时髦。更低的用车成本、更安静的车厢以及政府支持，让这个选择更容易。曾经看似冒险的购买，如今对许多家庭而言已是明智之选。

paragraphs.en: Battery technology explains much of the change. In 2010, a typical electric car could travel only about 100 miles on one charge. Today, many models offer a range of 250 to 400 miles, and fast charging can add most of that in under 40 minutes. Battery packs also cost far less than before. These improvements turned electric cars from city toys into vehicles that can handle weekend trips and family holidays.
paragraphs.zh: 电池技术解释了大部分变化。2010年，一辆典型电动汽车充一次电只能行驶约100英里。如今，许多车型续航可达250至400英里，快速充电能在40分钟内补足大部分电量。电池组成本也远低于从前。这些进步使电动汽车从城市玩物变成能胜任周末出游和家庭假期的车辆。

paragraphs.en: Charging infrastructure has grown quickly as well. In cities, shopping centers and office buildings now offer plugs; on highways, fast stations appear every few dozen miles. Many drivers simply charge at home overnight, waking up to a full battery. Yet the network is not even. Rural areas and older apartment blocks still lack convenient points, and long queues can appear during holiday travel.
paragraphs.zh: 充电基础设施也迅速增长。在城市，购物中心和写字楼现在提供充电插口；在高速公路上，快速充电站每隔几十英里就会出现。许多司机干脆在家过夜充电，醒来就是满电。然而，网络并不均衡。农村地区和老旧公寓楼仍缺乏便利的充电点，节假日出行时也可能排起长队。

paragraphs.en: Money matters, too. Electricity is usually cheaper than petrol per mile, and electric motors need less maintenance: no oil changes, fewer moving parts. Still, the first price of an electric car can be higher. That is changing as cheaper models arrive and the used market grows. For a young family, an affordable second-hand electric car may now cost about the same as a similar petrol model, while costing less to run.
paragraphs.zh: 钱也很重要。按每英里计算，电通常比汽油便宜，而且电动机需要的维护更少：不用换机油，活动部件更少。不过，电动汽车的初始价格可能更高。随着更便宜的车型上市和二手车市场扩大，这种情况正在改变。对一个年轻家庭来说，一辆负担得起的二手电动车如今价格可能与类似汽油车相当，而使用成本更低。

paragraphs.en: The environmental case is strong but not simple. Electric cars produce no tailpipe emissions, so city air becomes cleaner and streets quieter. When the electricity comes from wind, solar, or hydro power, the climate benefit grows. However, building batteries requires mining, and that has real costs. The goal is not to pretend those costs do not exist, but to manage them through recycling, better design, and cleaner power grids.
paragraphs.zh: 环境方面的理由充分，但并不简单。电动汽车没有尾气排放，因此城市空气更清洁，街道更安静。当电力来自风能、太阳能或水能时，气候效益更大。然而，制造电池需要采矿，这有实实在在的代价。目标不是假装这些代价不存在，而是通过回收、更好的设计和更清洁的电网来管理它们。

paragraphs.en: Problems remain. In cold weather, batteries lose part of their range, and drivers must plan longer stops. People living in apartments without private parking may struggle to charge overnight. Power grids also face pressure at peak hours. Engineers are testing battery swaps, smart charging that shifts demand to night, and roadside stations that combine coffee shops with fast plugs. None of these solves everything, but each makes the electric car easier to live with.
paragraphs.zh: 问题依然存在。寒冷天气下，电池会损失部分续航，司机必须规划更长的停靠。住在没有私人停车位的公寓里的人，可能难以过夜充电。电网在高峰时段也面临压力。工程师正在测试换电、把需求转移到夜间的智能充电，以及把咖啡馆和快速充电桩结合的路边站。这些都不能解决所有问题，但每一项都让电动汽车更易于日常使用。

paragraphs.en: The electric car era, then, is not a sudden revolution. It arrives through small routines: a cable by the door, a map that shows charging stops, a family comparing running costs at the kitchen table. Electric cars will not suit everyone tomorrow, and petrol models will stay for years. Yet the direction is clear. With better batteries, fairer prices, and smarter grids, the quiet car is becoming a normal part of a more sustainable road.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，电动汽车时代并非一场突如其来的革命。它通过小小的日常惯例到来：门边的一根充电线，一张显示充电站的地图，一家人在厨房桌边比较用车成本。电动汽车明天不会适合所有人，汽油车还会存在多年。然而方向是清楚的。随着更好的电池、更公平的价格和更智能的电网，安静的车正成为更可持续道路上的平常一部分。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Electric cars have become a practical part of daily life, although some challenges remain.
Electric cars will replace all petrol cars within the next five years.
Battery costs are the only reason why electric cars are selling well.
Governments should stop building charging stations in rural areas.
questions.explain: 文章从日常场景、销量、电池、充电、成本、环境与挑战等多方面说明电动车已进入日常生活，但仍面临充电不均、寒冷天气等问题。A最全面。B过于绝对，文中说汽油车还会存在多年。C以偏概全。D与文意相反。

questions.q: According to the passage, what helped make electric cars more practical?
options: Falling battery costs and longer driving range.
questions.explain: 第三段明确说电池成本下降、续航提升使电动车更实用。A和D与原文相反或无关，C文中未提。

questions.q: What can be inferred about charging infrastructure from paragraph 4?
options: It is now complete in every neighborhood.
It has improved but is still uneven in some areas.
It is only available in wealthy countries.
It is less important than battery size.
questions.explain: 第四段说充电设施增长快，但网络并不均衡，农村和老旧公寓仍缺便利充电点，节假日排长队。因此B正确。A、C、D均无依据。

questions.q: The word sustainable in paragraph 8 is closest in meaning to ______.
options: able to continue without harming the environment
questions.explain: sustainable意为“可持续的”，在文中指更环保、能长期维持的交通方式。A最接近。B、C、D与词义无关。
